title: Post Processing: Abundance and Distribution of Species in Open Vegetation Plots
author: Sabine St-Jean

steps.title: Download and Prepare Drone Imagery
steps.instruction: Download and organize drone photos for the 9 subplots of a given plot from Fulcrum and prepare them for annotation.

substeps.instruction: Download original small drone pictures from Fulcrum following: Vegetation Surveys: Herbs and Shrubs → Cover Estimates: Subplots → Subplots → Record [# from 1 to 9] → Vegetation Photos: Subplot → Download → Original.
Open the 9 pictures in a single PowerPoint file, assigning one slide per subplot.

steps.title: Annotate Species in PowerPoint
steps.instruction: Identify and label species on the images using the Fulcrum species list and canopy remarks.

substeps.instruction: Locate species using Fulcrum (Vegetation Surveys: Herbs and Shrubs → Subplot Record → Cover Estimates), noting direction acronyms (S=south, N=north, O/W=west, E=east, C=center) and individual counts.
For difficult-to-identify species, use a white font in PowerPoint to note the species initials (first letter of genus + first letter of species) on top of occurrences.
Save all PowerPoint slides as .tif files named in the format PlotNo.SubplotNo.

steps.title: Initialize SamplePoint Database
steps.instruction: Set up a plot-specific database in the SamplePoint program.

substeps.instruction: Create a database via Options ⟶ Database Wizard - Create DB.
Name the database using the site acronym and plot number (e.g., BOU# for Boucherville, MB# for Mer Bleue).
Populate the database by selecting all 9 annotated .tif/.tiff pictures (use 'Select All files' menu).
Open the database via Options ⟶ Select DataBase.

steps.title: Configure SamplePoint Classification Buttons
steps.instruction: Create and load a button file for species classification, ensuring all plot species are represented.

substeps.instruction: Create a new button file via Options ⟶ Custom Buttons ⟶ Create Custom Button Files (or load an existing site file via 'Load Existing' and edit).
Assign 4-letter uppercase names and descriptions (latin or common name; no single quotation marks) for each ground cover.
Ensure all species from the Fulcrum species list are included. If more than 30 species exist, use a button named 'Other' and manually note these species per subplot.
Always include buttons for 'Unknown', and if necessary, 'Ground', 'Water', or 'Dry'.
Load the completed file via Options ⟶ Custom Buttons ⟶ Load Custom Button File.

steps.title: Classify Subplot Imagery
steps.instruction: Use a 10x10 grid of crosshairs to classify species abundance in each subplot image.

substeps.instruction: Set grid size to 10x10 = 100 under Options ⟶ Select Grid Size.
Adjust image rotation (once per subplot), brightness, contrast, or zoom as needed. Compare SamplePoint images to Fulcrum originals to determine correct rotation (especially for subplot 5).
Click 'Begin' and classify each of the 100 red crosshairs by clicking the corresponding species button.
Reference the Fulcrum species list and original non-annotated picture on a separate monitor to assist identification.
After 100 points, click 'Next Image' then 'Begin' for the next subplot.
To resume interrupted work, use 'Next image' to find the subplot, enter the point number in the point field, and hit 'RST' (restart).

steps.title: Post-Classification Image Processing
steps.instruction: Finalize the visual records for the subplots.

substeps.instruction: Crop all photos into a tight square around the PVC pipes delimiting the subplot.
Save cropped photos back to the original Fulcrum subplot record or a shared Google Photos folder, labeled PlotNo.SubplotNo.

steps.title: Calculate Abundance in Excel
steps.instruction: Process the SamplePoint data in Excel to determine percent cover and species richness.

substeps.instruction: Combine all plot databases into one master file (keeping originals as backup).
Create a table with subplot numbers as the top row and species buttons as the left column.
Calculate relative abundance using the formula =COUNTIF(E$12:CZ$12, C23), where E$12:CZ$12 is the range of 100 buttons for the subplot and C23 is the species name.
Assign an abundance value of 0.5% to species listed in Fulcrum but not captured by the 100 SamplePoint crosshairs.
Add a row for the sum of relative abundances (must equal 100).
Add a row for the number of species per subplot using =COUNTIF(D22:D62, ">0").

steps.title: Generate Simplified Species Table
steps.instruction: Create a version of the species-per-dot table without RGB values.

substeps.instruction: Copy the image name column and point numbers row.
For each cell, use the formula =LEFT(E3,4) to keep only the first 4 characters of the original cell (E3), resulting in a table of 900 cells (100 points * 9 subplots).
